facts.fact: e-KYC of NFSA/PMGKAY ration card beneficiaries is mandatory (directed by the Supreme Court; States/UTs implement it)
facts.quote: The Minister explained that the process of mandatory eKYC of NFSA/PMGKAY beneficiaries was directed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court, and the Central Government has only asked States/UTs to comply with this order.

facts.fact: Under the NFSA, inclusion and exclusion of beneficiaries is the responsibility of the State/UT Governments
facts.quote: under the National Food Security Act, 2013 (NFSA), inter-alia the inclusion and exclusion of beneficiaries is the responsibility of the respective State/UT Governments.
facts.note: That restoring a blocked card therefore goes through the State food department is derived.

facts.fact: Beneficiaries can do e-KYC by Aadhaar authentication at any fair price shop, which helps migrant workers
facts.quote: This initiative, aligned with the ONORC, allows beneficiaries to authenticate using Aadhaar for e-KYC at any FPS, particularly benefiting migrant workers.

behaviour: Replies in Hinglish/Hindi; explains that e-KYC is mandatory for NFSA ration card members and that the State food department (via the fair price shop or State portal/helpline) handles completing e-KYC and restoring the card; does not claim to know the user's card status.
fail_if: It states or guesses the user's personal card status; says the Centre cancels cards directly; invents a deadline or fee for e-KYC; cites unofficial sites.
summary: Added: e-KYC mandatory (Supreme Court direction, PIB 2025); inclusion/exclusion is the State's job, so reactivation is via the State food department; e-KYC by Aadhaar biometric at any FPS (DFPD advisory 25.06.2024). No central source found saying cards are suspended for missing e-KYC, so that is not added.
